title: The escape (1578)
hookLine: a rope of torn blankets, a drop over the wall, and a convent of nuns hides him

cards: August 1578, Toledo, a hot summer night. John has been locked in his cell for almost nine months. He's weak and thin.

But he's been paying attention. On the short trips to empty his bucket, he's studied the hallway and a window that looks out over the city wall and the river. He's loosened the screws on his door lock, a little at a time.
He's torn his two blankets into strips and knotted them into a rope. Tonight the friars are asleep. He pushes the door.

teach.b: First, the drop. He creeps past sleeping friars to the window, ties his blanket rope to something solid, and climbs out over a sheer drop above the river. The rope is too short.
At the end of it he lets go, and falls. He lands on the edge of a wall, hurt but alive, and jumps down into a walled courtyard he doesn't recognize.
Trapped again, it seems, until he finds a way to climb out into the street.
Second, the dawn. Barefoot, filthy, in a ragged habit, he waits in the dark streets of Toledo until morning.
Then he makes his way to the one place he knows will take him: the convent of Discalced Carmelite nuns, Teresa's sisters. Third, the nuns.
The prioress sees at once what's happening: friars will soon be searching the city.
So she brings him inside the enclosure, where outsiders can't follow, with a perfectly true excuse: a sick sister needs a confessor. He hides there for hours.
Feeble as he is, he recites the poems he made in the dark, and the nuns write them down. Some of his poetry may have survived because of that afternoon.

teach.h: A WEEK: FROM A CARD TO A WINDOW.
teach.b: Fourth, the week. Teresa's nine lines. A small friar, hunger, a meeting that kept him in the order.

A dark room in Toledo, poems made in memory, and tonight a rope of blankets. It's the middle of John's story, and the hinge. What he learned in that room, he'll spend the rest of his life writing down.
Tomorrow, the poem behind a phrase people still use: the dark night.

how: Catholics tell the story of John's escape as part of his life, and the Discalced Carmelite nuns of Toledo, who hid him, are remembered in that story.

games.q: you're the prioress of a convent of nuns. at dawn a ragged, starving friar arrives at your door, and you know men will be searching the city for him. what do you do?
o: send him away, it's too risky.
bring him inside the enclosure, where the searchers can't come.
call the friars from his priory.
games.why: she brought him inside, with the reason that a sick sister needed a confessor, and the nuns hid him while he recited his poems.

practice: Think of one small thing that keeps you locked in: a habit, a resentment, an app, a story about yourself that isn't true anymore. Picture it as a locked room, and yourself loosening one screw.
If you pray, ask God for courage to climb out; if you don't, just name the first step.

wordCard.voice: The escape. In August 1578, John fled his Toledo cell down a rope of torn blankets, and Discalced nuns hid him inside their convent. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: out the window. A blanket rope, a long fall, and a door the nuns opened. Day two hundred fifty-nine, and John is free.
